title: Verify claim/release bd invocations against a live ledger; add BOPS_INTEGRATION suite
description:
Three bd invocations in internal/intent were written from docs, not a live run:

  bd update <id> --claim --if-assignee ''     (empty-string CAS)
  bd update <id> --assignee ''                (clear assignee on release)
  bd label add|remove <id> <label>

Also capture real shapes for `bd show <id> --json` (one-element array?) and
`bd comments <id> --json` (needed by note/stale) into testdata/README.md as
field lists — never commit a real ledger export.

Approach: `bd init` in a temp dir, create two beads, run bops claim/release
through bdx.Exec, assert readback. Gate the suite on BOPS_INTEGRATION=1 so
`go test ./...` stays Dolt-free.

NEXT: run the suite locally with bd 1.3.2, then on a second machine after bd dolt pull.

written in SPEC.md. Children are sized for one Claude Code session each.

bops note (ending with a NEXT: paragraph) → bops release --reason done → PR.

title: sync: clear this run's ledger display when its claim ref is gone and nobody holds the bead
description: Found running the PROCESS §12 runbook on a scratch ledger (bops-ss6.22, 2026-11-10). When a run's claim ref is deleted and no other run takes it (a mistaken delete, or sweep of a ref the run still journalled), bops sync reports the bead in lost_claims and drops the hold, but the ledger keeps assignee=<actor>, status in_progress and the run: label. No one owns the bead, yet a plain claim refuses it and claim --force waits 120 minutes from updated_at. PROCESS §12 documents a manual clear (bd update --assignee '' --status open; bd label remove run:<ulid>; bops sync).
acceptance_criteria: When sync finds this run's held ref absent and the ledger still shows this run (assignee and run:<this run>), it clears the assignee, sets status open and removes the run: label, and still reports lost_claims; when another run holds the ref, sync leaves the display to that run. A test covers both cases, and the manual step in PROCESS §12 is removed or kept only for raw bd claims.
close_reason: sync now returns a bead to the pool when this run's claim ref is gone and nobody took it (in progress under this run's run: label, not landing); other runs, closed and landing beads untouched. Tests per case, each guard mutation-checked; replayed with real bd on a scratch ledger.

title: Report a missing Dolt remote in lock.mode ref from doctor and sync
description: Found in bops-b5c (PR #13). Claims in ref mode now refuse with remote_mismatch when there is no Dolt remote, but release, land, sweep and sync don't call checkRemote. In ref mode with no Dolt remote (a claim made before #13, or the Dolt remote removed later): sync and sweep fail at bd dolt pull ('no remote', exit 1); release deletes the ref then leaves the ledger pending with a warning; land succeeds silently because bd dolt push exits 0 'skipping'. Have doctor (which today never reads the Dolt remote list) and sync report the missing Dolt remote with the same fix advice as remote_mismatch, and decide whether land should warn.
acceptance_criteria: In ref mode with no Dolt remote, bops doctor reports a failing check naming the missing Dolt remote with both fixes (add a Dolt remote, or lock.mode none in .bops.json); sync's error or warning names the cause instead of the raw bd error; land warns that the ledger was not published; tests cover each; lock.mode none is unaffected.
close_reason: merged via https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/pull/14 (524e97a)

title: Refuse claims in lock.mode ref when no Dolt remote exists
description: Found while doing bops-q85 (PR #12). In lock.mode ref, checkRemote returns nil when the Dolt remote list is empty, so a repo with a git origin but no Dolt remote passes the remote check. The claim lock then runs with no ledger remote beside it, contrary to the design rule that the lock must live beside the ledger (SPEC §3.0, design doc 'the lock must live beside the ledger'); sync and claim --force only fail later at the publish step. Under lock.mode none this case is handled by q85's 'no Dolt remote: ledger not published' skip.
acceptance_criteria: In lock.mode ref with a git lock remote and an empty Dolt remote list, claim (and claim --force) refuse before any ref push with a stable code (reuse remote_mismatch, or justify a new one in SPEC); lock.mode none is unaffected; a test covers both modes; SPEC's stable-code text says so.
close_reason: merged via https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/pull/13 (4bd8fcc)

title: Infer the forge from lock.remote instead of origin
description: bops/internal/forge/forge.go infers the forge from 'git remote get-url origin'. Since PR #8 the lock can live on a remote named by lock.remote, so a repo whose lock remote is not origin may infer the wrong forge (or none). Use the configured lock remote (or decide forge selection should stay tied to origin and document why).
acceptance_criteria: With lock.remote set to a non-origin remote and no forge config, forge inference reads that remote; a test covers it; SPEC's forge-selection sentence is updated.
close_reason: merged via https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/pull/11 (65f72ca)

title: Treat no Dolt remote as nothing to publish under lock.mode none
description: Under lock.mode none (PR #9) claim treats a failed Dolt pull/push as a warning, but release (ledger_pending), land (exit 1 'push failed'), sweep, sync and session-start still treat a failed bd dolt pull/push as an error. A single-machine repo with no Dolt remote at all will hit those failures. Decide and implement: when no Dolt remote is configured, skip publishing with a note instead of failing.
acceptance_criteria: In a repo with no Dolt remote and lock.mode none, release, land, sweep, sync and session-start succeed without a publish error; with a Dolt remote configured, a failed push still fails as today; tests cover both.
close_reason: merged via https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/pull/12 (a48be07)

title: Draft a comment for beads#8282 with measured race and lock results

comments.author: Alex Nelson
comments.text: Draft written and shown to the owner on 2026-11-11 (session scratchpad: beads-8282-comment-draft.md). Not posted; awaiting owner review.

comments.author: Alex Nelson
comments.text:
Thanks for writing this up. We hit the same race and can add some data, plus the workaround we built in the meantime.

**What we observed (bd 1.3.4)**

In a two-replica test (two clones, one git remote) we ran `bd update <id> --claim` on both replicas at once. Both claims succeeded locally. A's `bd dolt push` succeeded and B's was rejected. B then ran `bd dolt pull`, Dolt settled `assignee` last-write-wins in B's favour, and B pushed. This happened in both of the runs we did. Both replicas were on one machine, so this shows the race exists, not how often it happens on a real network.

Your report mentions the notices that `pull` prints. In our sequence the side that pulls is the side that wins, so the notice goes to the winner. The replica that was told its claim succeeded (A) never pulls a conflict and is never told it lost. `--if-assignee` / `--if-status` don't help, because they compare and set on one replica too, and `bd update --claim` refuses to combine with them.

**Workaround: a git-ref claim lock** ([design](https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/blob/3a9f2bc81312d7cdcffe5c73ab8b5013971ee7d9/docs/designs/bops-claim-lock-v0.1.0.md), [ADR amendment](https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/blob/3a9f2bc81312d7cdcffe5c73ab8b5013971ee7d9/docs/adr/0001-derived-read-model-not-write-path.md#amendment-2026-11-10-a-git-ref-claim-lock))

Each bead gets one ref, `refs/bops/claims/<id>`, on the same remote as `refs/dolt/data`. It is written with `git push --force-with-lease=<ref>:<expected>` (an empty `<expected>` for a create-only push), so the forge's ref update is the compare-and-set. Exactly one machine wins. The loser exits non-zero before touching the ledger. The ref holds only run, actor, state, nonce and timestamp, never issue data, and `bd update --claim` is still written afterwards so people and tools that read the ledger can see who holds the bead.

Measured:
- Raw git on GitHub, two clones pushing at once: exactly one winner in 40 of 40 create-only races and 20 of 20 leased-replace (takeover) races ([results](https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/blob/3a9f2bc81312d7cdcffe5c73ab8b5013971ee7d9/bops/testdata/README.md#git-ref-lock-on-github-git-2560-2026-11-09)).
- End to end against real bd 1.3.4 in CI (two clones, a local bare remote, one runner): 40 races with distinct actors and 40 with one shared actor. Every trial ended with exactly one `claimed` and one `lost`. Claim latency was p50 2.26 s / max 4.33 s and p50 2.02 s / max 2.66 s respectively ([test](https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/blob/3a9f2bc81312d7cdcffe5c73ab8b5013971ee7d9/bops/cmd/bops/replica_test.go), [CI run](https://github.com/extremenelson/beads-ops/actions/runs/42954571258)). Forty clean trials only bound the failure rate to roughly 7.5% at 95% confidence. The guarantee rests on the server's leased push, not on the trial count.

Costs:
- It is a second write path just for ownership, and it covers only claims made through our wrapper. A raw `bd update --claim` bypasses it.
- A claim now needs the network. Offline claims are refused.
- It needs a forge that accepts custom refs with `--force-with-lease`. We have only measured GitHub.
- Each lock commit needs a nonce. Pushing an identical object reports success to both sides.
- About 2 s per claim in our CI.

We plan to delete the lock the day bd can do this itself.

**The ask**

A cross-replica compare-and-set on claim: a `bd update --claim` (or `bd ready --claim`) that, when a remote is configured, either wins against the remote or fails with a distinct exit code, instead of succeeding locally and being settled last-write-wins later.

If that doesn't fit the Dolt model, any one of these would let tools build it without a side channel:
1. A conditional push: `bd dolt push` that refuses, rather than merging, when a named cell (here `assignee`) changed on the remote since the local base.
2. A machine-readable report from `bd dolt pull` of which local writes lost last-write-wins (issue id, field, local and winning values), so the loser can be told.
3. Confirmation that the `expectedRevision` compare-and-swap on the ROADMAP (#6136) will be checked against the remote and not only the local replica, which would cover this.

Happy to test a branch against the suite above.

comments.author: Alex Nelson
